Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:10:1.hebrew: וכי תימא נילף - כסף קידושיה מכסף קנסה, שאונס ופתוי לאביה חמשים כסף:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:10:1.english: And if you would say: Let us derive - Her betrothal money from the money of her fine, for [the fine for] rape and seduction [paid] to her father is fifty [shekels of] silver.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:10:2.hebrew: ממונא מקנסא לא ילפינן - שהקנס כולו חידוש, ומחידוש לא גמרינן. ואכתי, קידושיה מנלן דלאביה הוי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:10:2.english: We do not derive monetary matters from fines - For the fine is entirely a novelty, and from a novelty we do not derive [other laws]. And still, from where do we [derive] that her betrothal [money] belongs to her father?

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:11:1.hebrew: מבושת ופגם - דקיימא לן בכתובות (דף מ:) שהמאנס נותן בושת ופגם לאב, והנהו לאו קנסא נינהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:11:1.english: From humiliation and degradation - For we maintain in Ketubot (40b) that a rapist pays [compensation for] humiliation and degradation to the father, and those are not a fine.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:11:2.hebrew: דאבוה שייך בגוייהו - שיש לו דין חלק בהן, שיש בידו לביישה ולפוגמה בשביל ממון שיתנו לו, דאי בעי מסר לה למנוול ומוכה שחין, דהויא לה בושת ופגם. ואנס זה שבא עליה מחסר ממון זה, שזילזלה, ולא יקפצו עליה תובעין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:11:2.english: As her father has an interest in them - For he has a legal right to a share in them, as it is in his power to humiliate her and degrade her for the sake of money that they would give him; for if he wishes, he [could] give her [in marriage] to a repulsive man or one afflicted with boils, which would be humiliation and degradation for her. And this rapist who violated her causes a loss of this money, because he debased her, and suitors will not eagerly come forward for her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:12:1.hebrew: אלא - לעולם מקרא קמא ד״אין כסף לאדון זה״ נפקא. ודקשיא לך: ״ואימא לדידה״ — מסתברא דלאביה, דכי קממעט יציאת אירוסין מדין יציאת אמה העבריה, ובא לומר: כאן אין כסף, אבל ביציאת אירוסין יש כסף:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:12:1.english: Rather - Actually, it is derived from the first verse, [stating] that "there is no money for this master." And as for your difficulty: "And say [the money belongs] to her" — it is reasonable that [it belongs] to her father, for when it excludes the departure of betrothal from the law of the departure of a Hebrew maidservant, and comes to say: "Here there is no money, but in the departure of betrothal there is money."

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:1:1.hebrew: לא מקניא נפשה - דגנאי הוא לה. הלכך, בטיל לה לתורת חליפין בקידושין. ואפילו בכלי שיש בו שוה פרוטה, אי יהיב לה בלשון חליפין — עד דיהיב לה בתורת לשון קנין או קיחה או קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:1:1.english: She does not allow herself to be acquired - For it is degrading to her. Therefore, the legal mechanism of ḥalifin is void regarding betrothal; and even with a vessel that is worth a peruta, if he gives [it] to her with the language of ḥalifin, [it is ineffective] unless he gives [it] to her under the rubric of the language of acquisition, or taking, or betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:2:1.hebrew: מה יבמה שאינה יוצאה בגט - דילפי' לקמן בהאי פרקין (קידושין דף יד.), כתיב: ״לה״ — ולא ליבמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:2:1.english: Just as a yevama, who is not released through a bill of divorce - As we derive later in this chapter (Kiddushin 14a): It is written, "[and he shall write] her" — and not a yevama.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:4:1.hebrew: בכסף מנלן - הכא עיקר, ולעיל (קידושין דף ב.) אגב גררא נקיט ליה לתרוצי לשון קנין דמתני':
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:4:1.english: With money: From where do we [derive it]? - Here is the primary [place], and earlier (Kiddushin 2a) [the Gemara] brought it in passing to resolve the language of acquisition in the mishna.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:4:2.hebrew: זכאי בבתו - שהכסף יהיה שלו, והוא מקבל השטר, והוא מוסרה לביאה על כרחה לשם קידושין, בעודה נערה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:4:2.english: Has authority over his daughter - That the money shall be his, and he receives the document, and he hands her over for sexual intercourse against her will for the purpose of betrothal, while she is still a young woman.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:4:3.hebrew: מנלן - הנך תרתי: דמקניא בכסף כדקתני מתני', ומנלן שהאב זכאי בו כדקתני התם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:4:3.english: From where do we [derive this]? - [The Gemara is asking about] these two [matters]: that [a woman] is acquired with money, as our mishna teaches; and from where do we derive that the father is entitled to it [the money], as [the mishna] teaches there.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:5:1.hebrew: ויצאה חנם - גבי אמה העבריה היוצאת מרשות אדון בסימני נערות. ומצי למיכתב ויצאה חנם, ולא בעי אין כסף, אלא למידרש ביה: אין כסף לאדון זה שיוצאה ממנו, אבל יש כסף לאדון אחר כשיוצאה ממנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:5:1.english: And she shall go out free - [This is stated] regarding a Hebrew maidservant who leaves the authority of [her] master upon [developing] the signs of maidenhood. And [the verse] could have written "and she shall go out free," and would not have needed "without money"; rather, [it was written] in order to derive from it: There is no money for this master from whom she leaves, but there is money for another master when she leaves him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:6:1.hebrew: ואימא לדידה - הוי האי כסף, דהא לא כתיב ״אין לו כסף״ דתידוק מינה: ״אין כסף לאדון זה כו'״, אלא הכי דוק מינה: ״אין כסף ביציאה זו, אבל יש כסף ביציאה אחרת״ — ולעולם לדידה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:6:1.english: And say [it belongs] to her - Let this money belong [to her], for it is not written, "There is no money for him," that you would deduce from it: "There is no money for this master, etc."; rather, deduce from it as follows: "There is no money in this departure, but there is money in another departure" — and [the money could] actually [belong] to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:6:2.hebrew: ואיהי תשקול כספא - בתמיה: אפשר שעל חנם זיכהו הכתוב בקבלת קדושיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:6:2.english: And she should take the money - [This is said] in astonishment: Is it possible that Scripture granted him [the father] the right to receive her betrothal for nothing?

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:7:1.hebrew: ואימא ה"מ - דזכי ליה לקבלם בקטנה, שאין לה יד, דלאו בת דעה היא. ואע"ג דקרא דמוציא שם רע בנערה כתיב — דכתיב (דברים כ״ב:י״ט) ונתנו לאבי הנערה — לעולם דקדשה ניהלה בקטנותה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:7:1.english: And say these matters [apply] - That [Scripture] granted him [the right] to receive them [i.e., her betrothal] in [the case of] a minor [girl], who has no [legal] hand, as she is not of [mature] understanding. And even though the verse of the defamer is written regarding a young woman — as it is written: (Deuteronomy 22:19) "and they shall give [them] to the father of the young woman" — actually, [it refers to a case where] he betrothed her to him during her minority.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:7:2.hebrew: אבל נערה דאית לה יד - משהביאה שתי שערות, גדולה לכל דבר — לכל עונשין ולממון, שמקחה מקח וממכרה ממכר — איהי תקדיש נפשה כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:7:2.english: But a young woman, who has legal capacity - Once she has grown two [pubic] hairs, [she is] an adult in every respect — for all punishments and for monetary matters, in that her purchase is a [valid] purchase and her sale is a [valid] sale — [therefore,] let her betroth herself, etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:7:3.hebrew: בנעוריה בית אביה - הכי דריש לה: כל זמן שבנעוריה, היא של אביה, דכל שבח הבא לה לאביה הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:7:3.english: In her youth, in her father's house - This is how [the verse] is expounded: As long as [she is] in her youth, she belongs to her father, for any gain that comes to her belongs to her father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:8:1.hebrew: לאמה - קרא יתירא הוא, ודריש ליה: בתו הרי היא לו כאמה. ובבתו נערה אשמעי', דאי בקטנה לא איצטריך — השתא זבוני מזבין לה, מעשה ידיה מבעיא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:8:1.english: As a maidservant - It is a superfluous phrase, and he expounds it: His daughter, behold she is to him like a maidservant. And it teaches us [this] regarding his daughter [who is] a young woman, for if [it were] regarding a minor, it would not be necessary — now, [if] he can sell her, is [his right to] her earnings in question?!

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:8:2.hebrew: תיפוק ליה מבנעוריה - אי מיניה הוי מצי למילף, אלא על כרחך, מדלא יליף מהתם, שמעינן מינה: לא לשבח נעורים אתיא, דלגופיה איצטריך גבי נדרים דקאי עלייהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:8:2.english: Let him derive it from “in her youth” - If he could have derived [it] from it [he would have done so]; but perforce, since he did not derive [it] from there, we learn from this that it does not come for the profit of youth, for it was needed for itself, regarding the vows that it refers to.

Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:9:1.hebrew: וכי תימא נילף - ממון מנדרים — ממונא מאיסורא כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 3b:9:1.english: And if you would say: Let us derive - [I.e., derive] monetary matters from [the law of] vows — [to which the Gemara responds:] "Monetary matters from ritual prohibitions, etc."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:11:1.hebrew: וכי תימא נילף מבושת ופגם - תימה: היכי בעי למימר נילף קידושין מבושת ופגם? הא בושת ופגם גופה לא ידעינן שהן לאב אלא מקידושין, דאמר בסוף אלו נערות (כתובות דף מ:): דאי בעי מסר לה למנוול ומוכה שחין! וכ"ת דנ"מ מיהא דאי בעי מסר לה כשהיתה קטנה והיה עומד לה בושת זה אף בנערות — א"כ, גם כשהיא בוגרת יהא בושת ופגם של אב מהאי טעמא! וי"ל: דלא דמי בוגרת לנערות, דנהי דלא ילפינן מהפרת נדרים כולה מלתא, לענין הא ילפינן שלא ימשוך כח האב אלא ימי נערות, כי ההיא דלקמן: ומה סימנין שאין מוציאין מרשות אב מוציאין מרשות אדון, בגרות שמוציאה כו'. ומנא לן הא דבגרות מוציא מרשות אב לקידושין ולכל דבר אי לאו דילפינן מהפרת נדרים? מיהו לא נהירא, כיון דבטעמא תליא מלתא דאי בעי מסר לה בקטנות, כך שייך דבר זה לבגרות כמו לנערה. לכן נ"ל: לעיל, ואימא ה"מ קטנה — כלומר, קטנה שייך לעשות אותו ק"ו: דהשתא אביה מקבל קדושיה, איהי תשקול כספא?! כיון שאין לה כלל יד לקדש עצמה; אבל נערה, דאית לה יד, איהי תקדיש נפשה ותשקול כספא! פירוש: כיון דיש לה יד לקדש עצמה, יהיו הקידושין שלה; אבל אמת הוא שגם כשהיא נערה אביה יכול לקדשה, וכשאביה מקדשה אז יהיו הקידושין שלו. והשתא ניחא קושיא דלעיל, דקרא איירי כשקדשה אביה, והתם יליף בושת ופגם מקידושין שע"י אביה שהם של אביה. והכא ה"ק: וכי תימא נילף מבושת ופגם — קידושין שע"י עצמה, שיהא של אביה מבושת ופגם; כי ודאי מקדושי אביה ליכא למילפינהו, שאלו על ידה לגמרי הם; אבל מתחילה הוה יליף בושת ופגם, שאינו על ידה, מקדושי אביה, ובתר הכי איכא למילף מה שהוא על ידה ממה שאינו על יד אביה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:11:1.english: "And if you would say: Let us derive [it] from humiliation and degradation" - This is astonishing: How can [the Gemara] say, "let us derive betrothal from humiliation and degradation"? Behold, regarding humiliation and degradation itself, we do not know that they belong to the father except from betrothal, as [the Gemara] states at the end of [the chapter] Elu Na'arot (Ketubot 40b): "For if he wished, he could give her [in marriage] to a repulsive man or one afflicted with boils"! And if you would say that it is derived, at any rate, from [the fact] that if he wished, he could have given her [in marriage] when she was a minor, and this humiliation would have persisted for her even into young womanhood — if so, even when she is a mature woman (bogeret), humiliation and degradation should belong to the father for this [same] reason! And one could say that a bogeret is not comparable to young women (na'arot): for although we do not derive the entire matter from the nullification of vows, regarding this [point] we do derive that the father's authority does not extend beyond the days of young womanhood, like that [passage] below (4a): "And if [pubertal] signs, which do not remove [a daughter] from the authority of her father, remove [a maidservant] from the authority of her master, then bagrut (full maturity), which removes [her from her father], etc." And from where do we know that bagrut removes [a daughter] from her father's authority with regard to betrothal and all matters, if not that we derive it from the nullification of vows? However, this is not satisfactory: since the matter depends on the rationale that if he wished, he could have given her [in marriage] in childhood, this applies to a bogeret just as to a na'arah. Therefore, it seems to me: Above, [when the Gemara said,] "And say these words [apply to] a minor girl" — that is to say: for a minor girl, it is appropriate to make that a fortiori argument: "Now that her father receives her betrothal, shall she take the money?!" — since she has no legal agency whatsoever to betroth herself. But a young woman (na'arah), who does have legal agency, let her betroth herself and take the money! Explanation: Since she has legal agency to betroth herself, the betrothal [money] should be hers. However, the truth is that even when she is a na'arah, her father is able to betroth her, and when her father betroths her, then the betrothal [money] belongs to him. And now the difficulty above is resolved: for the verse deals with when her father betrothed her, and there [in Ketubot 40b], it derives humiliation and degradation from betrothal [effected] through her father, which belongs to her father. And here, this is what [the Gemara] is saying: "And if you would say: Let us derive from humiliation and degradation" — [meaning,] that betrothal [effected] through herself shall belong to her father from humiliation and degradation; for certainly from the betrothal [effected by] her father one cannot derive them, as these are entirely by her own agency; but initially, it derived humiliation and degradation, which are not [brought about] by her agency, from betrothal [effected by] her father, and after that, it is possible [to suggest] to derive that which is by her agency from that which is not by her father's agency.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:3:1.hebrew: ואין דבר אחר כורתה - וא"ת: תהא אמה העבריה יוצאה בחליצה מק"ו דיבמה, מהאי ק"ו גופה! ואין לומר "אשה תוכיח" — דמה לאשה שכן אינה יוצאה בכסף, תאמר באמה? וי"ל: דה"א שפחה כנענית תוכיח, דיוצאה בכסף ואין יוצאה בחליצה. וא"ת: היא גופא תיתי בהאי ק"ו דתיפוק בחליצה! וי"ל: דאיכא למיפרך, מה ליבמה שיוצאת במיתת היבם ולכך יוצאת בחליצה, תאמר בשפחה כנענית שכן אינה יוצאה במיתת אדון, לכך אינה יוצאה בחליצה! וא"ת: א"כ, היכי נימא "שפחה כנענית תוכיח"? איכא למיפרך: מה לשפחה כנענית שכן אינה יוצאה במיתת אדון, תאמר באמה העבריה! וי"ל: דנעשה יוכיח מאשה ומשפחה כנענית: דכי פרכת מה לשפחה כנענית שכן אינה יוצאה במיתת אדון — אשה תוכיח, שיוצאה במיתת הבעל ואינה יוצאה בחליצה; מה לאשה שכן אינה יוצאה בכסף — שפחה כנענית תוכיח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:3:1.english: “And nothing else severs her” - And should you say: Let a Hebrew maidservant be released through ḥalitza by an a fortiori inference (kal vaḥomer) from a yevama, from this very kal vaḥomer itself! And one cannot say: Let [a married] woman prove [otherwise] — for what [can be deduced from a married] woman, who is not released with money; can you say [the same] of a [Hebrew] maidservant? And one can say: That we would say: A Canaanite maidservant will prove [otherwise], for she is released with money, and yet is not released through ḥalitza. And if you say: Let she herself [the Canaanite maidservant] be derived through this kal vaḥomer, that she should go free through ḥalitza! And one can say: That it can be refuted: What [can be inferred from] a yevama? For she is released upon the death of the yavam, and therefore she is released through ḥalitza; can you say [the same] of a Canaanite maidservant, who is not released upon the death of [her] master, therefore she is not released through ḥalitza! And if you say: If so, how can we say [that] a Canaanite maidservant will prove [otherwise]? One can refute [this]: What [about] a Canaanite maidservant, who is not released upon the death of [her] master; can you say [the same] of a Hebrew maidservant! And one can say: That we construct a [combined] proof from [a married] woman and a Canaanite maidservant: For when you refute, "What [about] a Canaanite maidservant, who is not released upon the death of [her] master?" — [a married] woman will prove [otherwise], for she is released upon the death of the husband, and yet is not released through ḥalitza; [and when you refute,] "What [about a married] woman, who is not released with money?" — a Canaanite maidservant will prove [otherwise].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:4:1.hebrew: האב זכאי בבתו וכו' - מפרש בירושלמי שיש לו זכות בביאה — שנותנין לו שכר לקדש בביאה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:4:1.english: "A father has authority over his daughter, etc." - It is explained in the Yerushalmi that he has a right with regard to intercourse — that they give him payment to betroth [her] through intercourse.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:6:1.hebrew: ואימא לדידה - וא"ת: הא ע"כ לא איצטריך קרא אלא לומר שהן לאב, דהא דמקדשה בכסף גמר קיחה קיחה משדה עפרון? וי"ל: דמ"מ מיתורא לא נאמר שהן של אב אם אין משמעות דקרא, דלקמן במסקנא אמרי' דהני תרי קראי צריכי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:6:1.english: "And say [it is given] to her" - And if you say: But perforce the verse was needed only to teach that they [the betrothal funds] belong to the father, for the fact that [a woman] is betrothed with money is derived from [the verbal analogy of] "taking" [and] "taking" from the field of Ephron! And one can say: Nevertheless, from a superfluity [alone] we would not say that they belong to the father if there is no indication in the verse; for later, in the conclusion, we say that these two verses are [both] needed.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:7:1.hebrew: ואימא ה"מ קטנה - אע"ג דקרא איירי בנערה, דכתיב (דברים כ״ב:ט״ז) "וסקלוה", ועוד דמוציא שם רע על הקטנה פטור — מ"מ י"ל דה"ק: "את בתי נתתי לאיש הזה" כשהיתה קטנה, ועתה היא גדולה. וא"ת: הא לקטנה לא איצטריך קרא, דהשתא זבוני מזבין לה — כסף קידושין מיבעיא?! דכה"ג אמרי' גבי מעשה ידיה בפרק נערה שנתפתתה (כתובות דף מז.). וי"ל: דלא דמי; דגבי מעשה ידיה ניחא, כי כשמכרה מוכר מעשה ידיה, שהרי למלאכתה נמכרת, אבל קידושין לא שייכא במכר. אע"פ שיכול ליעדה — היינו בכסף שנמכרה, אבל בקידושיה ממש לא מצינו שום זכות לאב. וא"ת: הא אמרינן בפרק נערה (שם) שמעשה הבת לאב מדזכי ליה רחמנא למימסרה לחופה, אע"פ שמבטלה ממלאכתה, ופירש התם בקונטרס דזכי ליה רחמנא מדכתיב "את בתי נתתי לאיש", דמשמע כל נתינות, אפילו מסירה לחופה; ומאי ראיה? אימא ה"מ קטנה, אבל נערה לא, כדאמר הכא! וי"ל: דהאי קרא "את בתי נתתי" ע"כ איירי בנערה כדפרישית; ונהי דלענין קידושין נוכל לפרש "את בתי נתתי" כשהיתה קטנה — החופה א"א לפרש אלא בנערה, דאי בקטנות — א"כ היתה נשואה כשזינתה, ודינה בחנק ולא בסקילה, דעל זנות של קטנות לא מיחייבה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 3b:7:1.english: And say this applies to a minor girl - Even though the verse is dealing with a young woman [na'arah] — as it is written: “and they shall stone her” (Deuteronomy 22:16 [v. 21]), and furthermore, one who defames a minor girl [ketannah] is exempt [from penalty] — nevertheless, one can say that this is what [the Gemara] means: [The father says,] “I gave my daughter to this man” [when] she was a minor, and now she is grown. And if you should say: But for a minor girl, a verse was not needed, for now [one can argue a fortiori]: he can sell her [into servitude], is [his right to her] betrothal money needed [to be taught by a verse]?! For we say similarly regarding her earnings in the chapter Na'arah SheNitpatetah (Ketubot 47a). And one can say: It is not comparable. For regarding her earnings it makes sense, because when he sells her, he sells her earnings, as she is sold for her labor; but betrothal does not belong to a sale. Even though [the master] can designate her [as a wife], that is with the money for which she was sold, but regarding her actual betrothal, we do not find any right of the father. And if you should say: But we say in the chapter Na'arah (ibid.) that the daughter’s earnings belong to the father because the Merciful One granted him [the authority] to hand her over to the chuppah, even though he thereby causes her to cease from her labor; and the Kuntres [Rashi] explained there that the Merciful One granted him [this authority] because it is written, “I gave my daughter to a man,” which implies all [forms of] giving, even handing over to the chuppah. And what is the proof? Say this applies to a minor girl, but to a young woman it does not, just as [the Gemara] says here! And one can say: This verse, “I gave my daughter,” must perforce be speaking of a young woman, as I explained. And granted that regarding betrothal we could explain “I gave my daughter” [as having occurred] when she was a minor; [the delivery to] the chuppah is impossible to explain other than [as having occurred] when she was a young woman. For if [she entered the chuppah] in her minority: if so, she would have been a fully married woman [nesu'ah] when she committed adultery, and her punishment would be by strangulation and not by stoning; for [if she committed adultery as a minor], one is not liable [to the death penalty] for adultery committed in minority.
